narrative.northStar: The Focused Dossier and Waypoint Rail
narrative.overview: Roleway feels like a personal operating system for deliberate career searches. The desktop shell leads with the account avatar, search, and create controls, then a Search Project switcher and grouped navigation beside one inset work surface. Today is a project-scoped action dossier; the Inbox is a keyboard-first triage surface; Opportunities combine grouped issue rows with composable and saved views; Contacts keeps people and follow-ups inside the active Search Project.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet workspace chrome surrounding one subtly inset, bordered work surface.
Neutral architecture with Waypoint Blue carrying primary actions, focus, selection, progress, and the route mark.
Document-like pages and record surfaces instead of dashboard card grids.
A first-class Search Project switcher keeps separate strategies, pipelines, and results distinct.
Navigation grouped by Focus, Prepare, and Review with one active blue waypoint.
Today leads with an ordered next-up list and a compact context rail.
Dark mode preserves the same semantic hierarchy.
Public pages use the real application shell and task-specific HTML views as product evidence.
The Inbox pairs a keyboard-navigable review queue with one listing dossier.
Opportunity filters compose in place and can be saved, renamed, applied, or removed.
Contacts expose relationship, Opportunity, and follow-up context in one compact list.
Mobile keeps primary destinations in the bottom bar and secondary routes in one More sheet.

rules.name: The One Saturated Voice Rule
rules.body: Waypoint Blue communicates forward action, focus, selection, progress, or a waypoint. Product chrome remains neutral.

rules.name: The Product Pin-up Rule
rules.body: Public pages get one dominant interface composition, one annotation system, and one tactile next-action object.

rules.name: The One Work Surface Rule
rules.body: One subtly inset, 12px work surface sits inside quiet sidebar chrome; internal content stays flat and avoids nested islands.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows explain hierarchy or movement; they never decorate static content.

dos: Do use proximity and hairlines before adding a container.
Do keep the next action and its due state visible near the record it affects.
Do reserve cards for movable opportunities, approvals, and self-contained records.
Do use Waypoint Blue for primary actions, focus, selection, progress, and the full Roleway route mark.
Do show real product structure and task-specific content on public pages.
donts: Don't add more than the single inset work surface or give every section its own floating island.
Don't tint application chrome blue or add secondary saturated colors, startup gradients, glass, glow, or decorative metrics.
Don't turn summaries into large dashboard cards or put empty-state icons in generic rounded tiles.
Don't copy Notion's brand assets or terminology.
Don't market Roleway with generic dashboard art, fake metrics, or product screenshots that show a discarded shell.
